notes: PARTIAL (2026-11-16, the 1985 code reads, rulings of batch 10): RECORD DELIMITER. The clause on a fixed-length file compiles with a warning only, and ANY word is taken as its implementor-name (`RECORD DELIMITER IS F1`, the file's own name, compiles) though the implementation defines none. See below: decided. Owner: kb/Work PB5844 (open). Ruled in kb/Work/PB5683/2026-11-16-rulings-code-reads-batch-10.md; the 1985 rows chained into this one: 1985-FMT-VII.2.8.2, 1985-GR-VII.2.8.4-3, 1985-GR-VII.2.8.4-5, 1985-SR-VII.2.8.3-1. The prose that follows is the stored account, kept as the account of the part that holds. || The general format is implemented EXACTLY as printed, and the printed page was rendered rather than inherited from the transcription (kb/Work PB292): RECORD, DELIMITER and STANDARD-1 are underlined (required words), IS is not (an optional word), feature-name-1 is a user-defined word, and the braces are a plain required choice of exactly one alternative with no choice indicators. `recordDelimiterClause : RECORD DELIMITER IS? (STANDARD_1 | cobolWord)` is that diagram one-for-one. All FOUR legal spellings are exercised by the golden and each draws the clause's named decline: STANDARD-1 with IS (file F1), feature-name-1 with IS (F2), STANDARD-1 with the optional word omitted (F3); the complement, a file with no clause at all (F4), draws none. The format row is CONFORMS rather than DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT because the syntax IS accepted here — §4.2.6 licenses accepting a declined processor-dependent element and only compels the warning, unlike Annex A.4.1, which forbids accepting an unclaimed OPTIONAL element's syntax (the A.4.8 FORMAT rows are DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT for that reason).
